cells.tense: The way through is in your hands right now, and you are walking it without a speech about it.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Take something you already understand and make the first real piece of it this week, with your hands, not a plan for it.
cells.core:
You can make a way plain for other people, and you can tell when your reading of a thing is good. Nobody had to point you to the passage. That is the shape of it going well: you know a thing, you put it where someone can walk on it, and you don't stand around waiting to be thanked.

What this week is free to feed is a thing you make. Take an understanding you already hold and build the first small piece of it, on the ground where the old version came down. No announcement, no fuller plan. One piece of the thing, real enough to touch by Friday. Building it is how the balance stays honest; the way you already find stays in your hands instead of getting traded for explaining.

cells.verb: charting the passage for whoever can't see the way yet
cells.place: where what you are is asking to be shown, not improved

cells.tense: You are bracing at the edge of next week, rehearsing a passage you have not walked yet.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: When a way of doing something stops fitting, put that method down and keep the purpose it served — once, and on purpose.
cells.core:
You can chart a passage for other people, and lately you are mapping the far end before the near one. Tomorrow's version of the thing is already built in your head, so the actual work looks like an obstacle to it. That is the excess: direction turns into pressure to arrive. Your attention goes to the distance instead of the road.

Let the friction do the testing. When an approach you've been carrying stops fitting, put it down and keep the aim it was serving. You are not losing the commitment. A purpose is tested by engagement — one difficult part, picked on purpose, one method set aside — and whatever survives that is what you actually meant. The passage opens when you stop insisting on the route.
cells.sheetLine: The route you rehearsed is not the purpose you started with.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed behind you seasons ago, holding a direction with no road on it.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Keep a private count of the small things you owe people, and pay one before you're asked, where only you can see it.
cells.core:
You can make a way plain for people, and right now you aren't pointed at anything. You have stopped arriving at what you were once walking toward. The direction isn't gone so much as unfollowed, and the one who holds it isn't entirely here. That happens when the ground under a person hasn't settled yet.

Charge the part of you that knows what is fair, not the part that finds the way. Keep a private tally of what you owe — a small debt, a hand you borrowed, a thing you said you'd do — and pay one item without being asked, no fanfare. What is owed is quieter than a direction and it doesn't need a road. Fairness gives you something to stand on before you ask yourself to lead anyone.
cells.sheetLine: What you owe is easier to find than where you are going.

cells.tense: You are steering the boat and telling everyone it is simply drifting with the current.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring one person into a piece of work you're carrying, so the two of you make it at the same time, neither going it alone.
cells.core:
You find the passage and show it, and you describe that as simply being practical. Anyone paying attention can see whose reading laid out the route, even when your telling skips that part. What's doing the work is direction from you, and the way you put it leaves you out of the boat.

The simpler form of the same thing: a passage you found gets followed together. Bring one person into a piece of work you're carrying, so the two of you hold it at once. Not a plan handed down. Two streams running as one, meeting in the middle. Saying that out loud keeps it genuine, and it stops leaving you outside your own course.
cells.sheetLine: The drift has a hand on the tiller, and the hand is yours.
cells.verb: charting the passage for whoever can't see the way yet
cells.place: where what you are is asking to be shown, not improved
